policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start every episode in A (press the first button). Apply the first matching rule, after updating memory for this step: 1. If the carried-in memory is empty and this step shows no execution frames (the very first decision step, gripper out of frame): A. 2. If buttons_pressed (after this step's update) is 1: B. A is executed at the first step only; at any step that shows execution frames, A has already been done, so if buttons_pressed is still 0 or 1 answer B (the frames showing the gripper lowered onto a button with closed fingers count as the first press). 3. If the scene at this decision step shows a container 'held in the gripper': D (put down the container). 4. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, and picked_colors is empty: C, pointing at the memory position (<color>_container) of the FIRST cube color named in the goal instruction (the one after 'hiding the'). Use the remembered container position, not the cube's original spot: the point is the <color>_container value written AT THIS STEP after the full chain, not the carried-in value; if the carried-in value still looks like a first-step cube position or has not been rewritten at a step showing containers, finish the memory update first and then point. 5. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, picked_colors has one entry, and the goal names a second cube ('another container hiding the ...'): C, pointing at the memory position of that SECOND color. This is the container that has not been lifted yet; do not point at the one just put down. The point is that color's value written at this step after the full chain, not the carried-in value. 6. If every cube named in the goal is already in picked_colors and nothing is held: the task is done; answer D. Fallback: if the needed color's memory position is unknown, point C at the container reached by chaining frame by frame from that cube's last known position as the memory instruction describes (after a swap a different container stands on the old spot, so do not take the nearest one); if no rule fits at all, answer the next unfinished item in goal order (A, B, C, D).

fields.name: buttons_pressed
fields.description: Write 0 at the first step (empty carried-in memory, no execution frames). Otherwise write the carried-in count plus 1 if any execution frame shown says a button 'is pressed down' OR shows the gripper at a button's [y, x] (within a few pixels) at height below about 0.06 with fingers closed; otherwise the carried-in count. e.g. 1

fields.name: green_container
fields.description: [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. At every step whose frames show containers, rewrite this field, and likewise red_container and blue_container, whether or not the color is named in the goal and whether or not its container moved. At the first step, with empty memory, WRITE the green cube's [y, x] from the scene. When containers first appear, take the container standing on the carried-in position. At every later step: (1) if the carried value is a cube position (first step with containers), take the container standing on it in the first frame shown; (2) otherwise take the container in the FIRST frame shown nearest the carried value, even if it is 10-15 px away because the glide was already under way; (3) step frame to frame, each time picking the container with the smallest displacement from the one just chosen; (4) write that container's last-frame position. Never match the carried value straight to the last frame. Mandatory joint procedure: (a) if any frame shows a container displaced from its position in the previous frame by more than a few pixels, run the chain for ALL THREE colors through every frame as a ONE-TO-ONE ASSIGNMENT: in each frame each container is assigned to exactly one color, so two fields can never end on the same container, and a container that one color leaves must be taken up by another color; (b) when the nearest candidate for one color is a near-tie (displacements within a few pixels of each other), choose the assignment that also gives the other colors a distinct nearest container with the smallest total displacement; (c) an identical container layout in the first and last frames of a step does not mean nothing moved; if middle frames show displacement, the result is usually a swap of two colors, and the chain decides which; (d) consistency check before writing: the three written values must be three different containers of the last frame, and if one field moved to a new container, the field that carried that container's old position must have moved too. Joint example: carried green [100, 166] and blue [130, 162]; frames show one container gliding [101, 168], [110, 178], [125, 182], [130, 163], [130, 160] while the other glides [130, 162], [121, 151], [106, 147], [102, 165], [101, 168]; write green_container=[130, 160] and blue_container=[101, 168], even if the goal names only one of them. Worked example of the swap trap: carried [131, 115]; first frame has containers at [118, 118] and [113, 162], pick [118, 118]; next frame it is at [99, 134], next at [101, 161]; write [101, 161], although the OTHER container, which came from [113, 162], now stands at [131, 116], almost exactly the carried value. A container standing in the last frame at the carried position is neither for nor against; only the chain decides. Conversely, when no container moves during a step, the chain returns the same container and the value stays (jitter of a few pixels aside). Containers gliding around each other usually finish swapped, but trust the chain, not the assumption (one circling pass swaps them, two passes return them). Write the followed container's position in the last frame. If any frame shows the green cube itself (container lifted or 'held in the gripper'), write the cube's position in the last frame it is visible, and keep that cube position at later steps even once a container is lowered back over it. e.g. [109, 126]

fields.name: red_container
fields.description: [y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly as green_container, rewritten at every step that shows containers even when red is not named in the goal and even when its container stood still (snapping from the cube's original position to the container on it): write the red cube's position at the first step; take the container that covers it; chain smallest-displacement matches from the first frame shown to the last (trust the chain, not an assumed swap; a last-frame container coinciding with the carried position is the swap trap, not a match), chained jointly with green and blue as a one-to-one assignment per frame, near-ties broken by consistency with the other chains, re-chained whenever any frame shows a container displaced even if the step's first and last layouts look identical, the three written values being three distinct last-frame containers. Example: carried red [112, 194] passes [121, 184], [119, 162] (chosen over [95, 182] because blue's chain takes that one), [103, 153], last frame [101, 152]; write [101, 152]; once the red cube is visible, its last visible position, kept after the container is set back down. e.g. [82, 152]

fields.name: blue_container
fields.description: [y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly as green_container, rewritten at every step that shows containers even when blue is not named in the goal and even when its container stood still (snapping from the cube's original position to the container on it): write the blue cube's position at the first step; take the container that covers it; chain smallest-displacement matches from the first frame shown to the last (trust the chain, not an assumed swap; never match the carried value straight to a last-frame container, even one standing within a pixel or two of it), chained jointly with green and red as a one-to-one assignment per frame, near-ties broken by consistency with the other chains, re-chained whenever any frame shows a container displaced even if the step's first and last layouts look identical, the three written values being three distinct last-frame containers. Example: carried blue [101, 152] passes [95, 163], [95, 182], [112, 194], last frame [114, 195]; write [114, 195]; once the blue cube is visible, its last visible position, kept after the container is set back down. e.g. [102, 79]

fields.name: picked_colors
fields.description: Written as the exact JSON text, double quotes, no spaces: [] at the first step and whenever empty, ["red"] after the red cube is exposed, ["red","green"] after both; a single-quoted list such as ['red'] is a mismatch. Carried-in list; append the color of a cube that appears visible beneath a lifted or 'held in the gripper' container among this step's frames, if that color is not already in the list. e.g. ["green"]
